input.useCase: A web app reads titles and content of Notion pages that each customer explicitly shares with this integration. Read content only. Never create or modify pages; no workspace administration.

coverage.action: Read titles of Notion pages that each customer explicitly shares with the integration
coverage.reason: The page object's title is a property; properties other than those marked with an asterisk require Read content. Execution is untested.

evidence.quote: Properties marked with an * are available to connections with any capabilities. Other properties require read content capabilities in order to be returned from the Notion API. For more information
Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve

coverage.action: Read content of Notion pages that each customer explicitly shares with the integration
coverage.reason: Reading data to export it out of Notion needs only Read content. Execution is untested.

evidence.quote: If your connection is reading data to export it out of Notion, your connection will only need Read content capabilities.

steps.title: Create the public connection with Read content only
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, configure the connection, set only the Read content capability, and record the client ID, client secret, and redirect URI for later use.
steps.doneWhen: Connection settings show Read content only, and the redirect URI and client credentials are recorded.

evidence.quote: Parameter Description Required client_id An identifier for your connection, found in the connection settings. ✅

steps.title: Implement the authorization redirect and code exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri, and response_type=code. Handle the callback code and error parameters. Exchange the code at the token endpoint using Basic auth and grant_type authorization_code. This is implementation only, not an executed flow.
steps.doneWhen: Callback handler and token exchange code exist and handle code and error responses.

Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .

steps.title: Authorize a test workspace with test pages
steps.detail: Using the developer's own test workspace and a test user, open the authorization URL, select a few test pages in the picker, and complete the redirect. Exchange the returned code for an access token.
steps.doneWhen: The token exchange returns an access token and the selected test pages are shared with the connection.

steps.title: Test reading a shared page title
steps.detail: Call the page retrieve endpoint with filter_properties=title using a shared test page ID. Expected: a page object whose properties include the title. Boundary: an unshared page should not return its title; the exact error is not in the supplied sources.
steps.doneWhen: A shared test page returns its title property, and an unshared page is not readable.

steps.title: Test reading shared page content as markdown
steps.detail: Call the markdown endpoint with a shared test page ID. Expected: a response containing the markdown string. Boundary: confirm that child content not shared with the connection is absent from the result.
steps.doneWhen: A shared test page returns markdown content, and unshared child content is not included.

evidence.quote: Permissions : The page contains child pages or other content that is not shared with the connection.

blockers.title: Verify public connection distribution and review requirements
blockers.resolution: Before customer rollout, check the Developer portal and Notion's public connection documentation for any review or distribution requirements. The supplied sources do not document them.

blockers.title: Confirm title retrieval behavior under Read content
blockers.resolution: During the title test, verify the title appears in the returned properties. The supplied sources imply this from the property-capability text but do not state it for the title explicitly.
